product: PREP BRAND ETHEPHON FOR COTTON AND TOBACCO

accepted.summary: Applicators and other handlers must wear specified personal protective equipment.
accepted.quote: Applicators and other handlers must wear coveralls over short-sleeved shirts and short pants, chemical resistant gloves made out of any waterproof material (barrier laminate, butyl rubber ≥ 14 mils, nitrile rubber ≥ 14 mils, neoprene rubber ≥ 14 mils, natural rubber ≥ 14 mils, polyethylene, polyvinyl chloride ≥ 14 mils, or viton ≥ 14 mils), chemical-resistant footwear plus socks, protective eyewear, chemical-resistant headgear for overhead exposure and chemical-resistant apron when cleaning equipment or mixing and loading.

accepted.applies_to: PREP™ brand Ethephon for Cotton and Tobacco
accepted.summary: Prohibition on applying via irrigation system.
accepted.quote: Do not apply PREP™ brand Ethephon for Cotton and Tobacco through any type of irrigation system.

accepted.summary: Recommendation to mix only daily expected usage.
accepted.quote: Mix only the amount of spray you expect to use each day.

accepted.summary: Prohibition on allowing mixed solution to stand overnight.
accepted.quote: Do not allow mixed solution to stand overnight.

accepted.summary: Prohibits applying the product in a way that contacts workers or other persons directly or through drift.
accepted.quote: Do not apply this product in a way that will contact workers or other persons, either directly or through drift.

accepted.summary: Requires that only protected handlers may be in the area during application.
accepted.quote: Only protected handlers may be in the area during application.

accepted.summary: Prohibits worker entry into treated areas during the restricted-entry interval (REI) of 48 hours.
accepted.quote: Do not enter or allow worker entry into treated areas during the restricted-entry interval (REI) of 48 hours.

accepted.applies_to: areas where average rainfall is less than 25 inches per year
accepted.summary: Specifies that the REI is 72 hours in areas where average rainfall is less than 25 inches per year.
accepted.quote: The REI is 72 hours in areas where average rainfall is less than 25 inches per year.

accepted.applies_to: early entry to treated areas involving contact with treated items
accepted.summary: Requires specific PPE for early entry: coveralls over long-sleeved shirt and long pants, chemical resistant gloves, chemical resistant footwear plus socks, and protective eyewear; adds chemical-resistant headgear for overhead exposure.
accepted.quote: PPE required for early entry to treated areas that is permitted under the Worker Protection Standard and that involves contact with anything that has been treated such as plants, soil or water is coveralls over long-sleeved shirt and long pants, chemical resistant gloves made of any waterproof material, such as nitrile, butyl, neoprene, or barrier laminate, chemical resistant footwear plus socks, and protective eyewear. For overhead exposure, chemical-resistant headgear is also required.

accepted.summary: Requires notifying workers orally and posting warning signs at entrances to treated areas.
accepted.quote: Notify workers of the application by warning them orally and posting warning signs at entrances to treated areas.

accepted.summary: Prohibits releasing spray at a height greater than 10 feet above the vegetative canopy unless necessary for pilot safety.
accepted.quote: Do not release spray at a height greater than 10 feet above the vegetative canopy, unless a greater application height is necessary for pilot safety.

accepted.summary: Requires use of a fine to medium or coarser droplet size (ASABE S572.1) for all applications.
accepted.quote: For all applications, applicators are required to use a fine to medium or coarser droplet size (ASABE S572.1).

accepted.summary: Prohibits boom length exceeding 65% of the wingspan for airplanes.
accepted.quote: The boom length must not exceed 65% of the wingspan for airplanes or 75% of the rotor blade diameter for helicopters.

accepted.summary: Prohibits boom length exceeding 75% of the rotor blade diameter for helicopters.
accepted.quote: The boom length must not exceed 65% of the wingspan for airplanes or 75% of the rotor blade diameter for helicopters.

accepted.summary: Requires using 1/2 swath displacement upwind at the downwind edge of the field.
accepted.quote: Applicators must use 1/2 swath displacement upwind at the downwind edge of the field.

accepted.summary: Requires orienting nozzles so spray is directed toward the back of the aircraft.
accepted.quote: Nozzles must be oriented so the spray is directed toward the back of the aircraft.

accepted.summary: Prohibits application when wind speeds exceed 10 miles per hour at the application site.
accepted.quote: Do not apply when wind speeds exceed 10 miles per hour at the application site.

accepted.summary: Prohibits application during temperature inversions.
accepted.quote: Do not apply during temperature inversions.

accepted.summary: Limits nozzle height to no more than 3 feet above the ground or crop canopy (manufacturer-recommended height allowed but not exceeding 3 ft).
accepted.quote: Apply with the nozzle height recommended by the manufacturer, but no more than 3 feet above the ground or crop canopy.

accepted.summary: Requires use of a fine to medium or coarser droplet size (ASABE S572.1) for all applications.
accepted.quote: For all applications, applicators are required to use a fine to medium or coarser droplet size (ASABE S572.1).

accepted.summary: Prohibits application when wind speeds exceed 10 miles per hour at the application site.
accepted.quote: Do not apply when wind speeds exceed 10 miles per hour at the application site.

accepted.summary: Prohibits application during temperature inversions.
accepted.quote: Do not apply during temperature inversions.

accepted.summary: Advises directing spray into the canopy.
accepted.quote: Direct spray into the canopy.

accepted.summary: The applicator is responsible for avoiding off-site spray drift.
accepted.quote: THE APPLICATOR IS RESPONSIBLE FOR AVOIDING OFF-SITE SPRAY DRIFT.

accepted.summary: Be aware of nearby non-target sites and environmental conditions.
accepted.quote: BE AWARE OF NEARBY NON-TARGET SITES AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS.

accepted.summary: Use the largest droplets that provide target pest control.
accepted.quote: Use the largest droplets that provide target pest control.

accepted.summary: Increasing the spray volume so that larger droplets are produced will reduce spray drift. Use the highest practical spray volume for the application.
accepted.quote: Increasing the spray volume so that larger droplets are produced will reduce spray drift. Use the highest practical spray volume for the application.

accepted.summary: If a greater spray volume is needed, consider using a nozzle with a higher flow rate.
accepted.quote: If a greater spray volume is needed, consider using a nozzle with a higher flow rate.

accepted.summary: Use the lowest spray pressure recommended for the nozzle to produce the target spray volume and droplet size.
accepted.quote: Use the lowest spray pressure recommended for the nozzle to produce the target spray volume and droplet size.

accepted.summary: Use a spray nozzle that is designed for the intended application. Consider using nozzles designed to reduce drift.
accepted.quote: Use a spray nozzle that is designed for the intended application. Consider using nozzles designed to reduce drift.

accepted.summary: Follow nozzle manufacturers’ recommendations for setting up nozzles. Generally, to reduce fine droplets, nozzles should be oriented parallel with the airflow in flight.
accepted.quote: Follow nozzle manufacturers’ recommendations for setting up nozzles. Generally, to reduce fine droplets, nozzles should be oriented parallel with the airflow in flight.

accepted.summary: For ground equipment, the boom should remain level with the crop and have minimal bounce.
accepted.quote: For ground equipment, the boom should remain level with the crop and have minimal bounce.

accepted.summary: Setting nozzles at the lowest effective height will help to reduce the potential for spray drift.
accepted.quote: Setting nozzles at the lowest effective height will help to reduce the potential for spray drift.

accepted.summary: Higher release heights increase the potential for spray drift.
accepted.quote: Higher release heights increase the potential for spray drift.

accepted.summary: Shielding the boom or individual nozzles can reduce spray drift. Consider using shielded sprayers.
accepted.quote: Shielding the boom or individual nozzles can reduce spray drift. Consider using shielded sprayers.

accepted.summary: Verify that the shields are not interfering with the uniform deposition of the spray on the target area.
accepted.quote: Verify that the shields are not interfering with the uniform deposition of the spray on the target area.

accepted.summary: When making applications in hot and dry conditions, use larger droplets to reduce effects of evaporation.
accepted.quote: When making applications in hot and dry conditions, use larger droplets to reduce effects of evaporation.

accepted.summary: Avoid applications during temperature inversions.
accepted.quote: Avoid applications during temperature inversions.

accepted.summary: AVOID APPLICATIONS DURING GUSTY WIND CONDITIONS.
accepted.quote: AVOID APPLICATIONS DURING GUSTY WIND CONDITIONS.

accepted.summary: Prepare only as much spray solution as can be used on the day of mixing.
accepted.quote: Prepare only as much spray solution as can be used on the day of mixing.

accepted.summary: Do not allow spray solution to stand overnight.
accepted.quote: Do not allow spray solution to stand overnight.

accepted.summary: Do not spill the concentrated product on spray equipment, or any airplane parts.
accepted.quote: Do not spill the concentrated product on spray equipment, or any airplane parts.

accepted.summary: Any spills should be rinsed immediately with plenty of water.
accepted.quote: ANY SPILLS SHOULD BE RINSED IMMEDIATELY WITH PLENTY OF WATER.

accepted.summary: Use of a nurse tank is highly recommended for avoiding possible spills of concentrated formulation on spray equipment or any airplane parts.
accepted.quote: Use of a nurse tank is highly re commended for avoiding possible spills of concentrated formulation on spray equipment or any ai rplane parts.

accepted.summary: For best performance, by ground or air application, choose equipment and spray volumes that will ensure uniform coverage of foliage and bolls.
accepted.quote: * For best performance, by ground or air application, choose equipment and spray volumes that will insure uniform coverage of foliage and bolls.

accepted.applies_to: aerial applications in California and Arizona
accepted.summary: In California and Arizona use a volume of no less than 5 gallons per acre for aerial applications.
accepted.quote: **** In California and Arizona use a volume of no less than 5 gallons per acre for aerial applications.

accepted.summary: annual max rate of ethephon active ingredient
accepted.quote: Do not exceed a maximum of 2. 0 lb. ethephon active ingredient per acre per year through combined or repeated uses of any ethephon products.

accepted.summary: prohibit tank mixing with desiccant for spindle-harvested cotton
accepted.quote: Boll Opening:  Do not tank mix PREP™ brand Ethephon for Cotton and Tobacco with a desiccant if the cotton is to be spindle harvested.

accepted.summary: prohibit tank mixing with desiccants unless plant desiccation is required
accepted.quote: Pre- Condition for Defoliation:  Do not tank mix PREP™ brand Ethe phon for Cotton and Tobacco with desiccants unless plant desiccation is required.

accepted.summary: do not use defoliant before sufficient mature unopened bolls exist
accepted.quote: Do no t use a defoliant before there is sufficient mature unopened boll s to produce the desired yield (see General Information section on how to test for boll maturity.

accepted.summary: do not apply if rain expected within 6 hours
accepted.quote: DO NOT APPLY PREP™ BRAND ETHEPHON FOR COTTON AND TOBACCO IF RAIN IS EXPECTED WITHIN 6 HOURS.  Rainfall within 6 hours of application may reduce product performance.

accepted.summary: do not plant another crop within 30 days after treatment
accepted.quote: Do not plant another crop within 30 days after treatment.

accepted.summary: harvest all leaves with 20% or more yellowing
accepted.quote: With a directed spray, be sure to harvest all leaves with 20% or more yellowing.

accepted.summary: use TG or OC spray tips designed to apply 50-60 gpa
accepted.quote: Choose TG or OC spray tips designed to apply 50 - 60 gpa at 35 -40 psi and at tractor speed of 2- 3 mph.

accepted.summary: use spray pressure of 40 to 60 psi
accepted.quote: Use a spray pressure of 40 to 60 psi.

accepted.summary: do not use additives other than recommended on label
accepted.quote: Do not use PREP™ brand Ethephon for Cotton and Tobacco with additives other than recommended on this label.

accepted.summary: use higher rate when temperatures are lower than normal
accepted.quote: Use the higher rate when the crop is heavy and has a tendency to be more rank or when temperatures are lower than normal.

accepted.summary: Treat when leaves are mature, not overly rank green.
accepted.quote: Successful results with PREP™ brand Ethephon for Cotton and Tobacco call for treatment when leaves are mature, not overly rank green when sprayed.

accepted.summary: Test spray several plants in more than one location in each field to determine proper treatment timing and number of leaves per stalk ready for harvest.
accepted.quote: To easily determine the proper treatment timing and the number of leaves per stalk ready for harvest, test spray several plants in more than one location in each field and observe the response.

accepted.summary: Leaves that fail to yellow in 72 hours are not mature and are not ready for treatment.
accepted.quote: Test leaves that fail to yellow in 72 hours are not ma ture and are not ready for PR EP™ brand Ethephon for Cotton  and Tobacco treatment.

accepted.summary: Harvest any yellowed leaves prior to application to avoid quality loss and/or possible leaf drop.
accepted.quote: To avoid quality loss and or possible leaf drop, harvest any yellowed leaves prior to application.

accepted.summary: Use lower rates under most conditions.
accepted.quote: Use lower rates under most conditions.

accepted.summary: Limit use of higher rates to cool (below 65°F at the time of treatment) slow ripening conditions.
accepted.quote: Limit use of higher rates to cool (below 65°F at the time of treatment) slow ripening conditions.

accepted.summary: Determine the number of acres to treat based on the confirmed number of leaves per plant that will color to fill the barn.
accepted.quote: When you have confirmed the desired number of leaves per plant that will color, you can determine the number of acres to treat in order to fill the barn.

accepted.summary: Prepare test spray by mixing one teaspoon of product in 1 quart of water.
accepted.quote: Prepare your test spray by mixing one teaspoon of PREP™ brand Ethephon for Cotton and Tobacco in 1 quart of water.

accepted.summary: Spray each test plant with about 1 oz. of the test mixture, covering all leaves with a fine mist.
accepted.quote: Spray each test plant with about 1 oz. of this mixture, covering all leaves with a fine mist.

accepted.summary: Harvest can commence 48 hours after application.
accepted.quote: Harvest can commence 48 hours after PREP™ brand Ethephon for Cott on and Tobacco application.

accepted.summary: Closely monitor treated crop and weather conditions to determine harvest timing and avoid quality loss or leaf drop.
accepted.quote: To determine harvest timing and avoid quality loss or leaf drop, closely monitor treated crop and weather conditions.
